title: Orbital-Selective Coexistence of Interlayer Spin-Singlet Formation and SDW Order with Anomalous Spin Reconfiguration in Bilayer Nickelate La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$ Revealed by $^{17}$O-NMR
authors: H. Lee, M. Yashima, M. Kakoi, T. Ino, Y. Arai, K. Kitagawa, H. Sakurai, Y. Takano, K. Kuroki, H. Mukuda
abstract: The spin structure of the spin density wave (SDW) order in the bilayer nickelate La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ has been investigated using site-selective $^{17}$O-NMR measurements on the inner apical O(1), outer apical O(2), and planar O(3,4) sites. Below $T_{\rm SDW}$ (= 150 K), the peak of all planar O(3,4) sites significantly broadens due to the emergence of a finite internal magnetic field, whereas O(2) sites remain with no (or a negligibly small) internal field. These results are consistent with commensurate SDW order with a single spin-spinless (or large-tiny spin) stripe. As for the O(1) sites that bridge the NiO$_2$ planes, the internal field is nearly canceled below $T_{\rm SDW}$, indicating an antiparallel spin configuration between adjacent planes. However, below $T_\text{A}$ ($\sim$ 115 K), the spectrum of the O(1) site disappears even though the in-plane SDW order remains robust, implying that the antiparallel spin configuration through the Ni--O(1)--Ni bond is not particularly stable below $T_{\rm A}$, despite the expected strong interlayer spin coupling between the NiO$_2$ planes. Above all, we emphasize that the local spin susceptibility is extremely small at the O(2) site that has a strong covalency with the $d_{3z^2-r^2}$ orbital, indicating a well-developed interlayer spin-singlet formation in the Ni-$d_{3z^2-r^2}$ orbitals bridging the NiO$_2$ planes. These findings shed new light on the interlayer spin-singlet formation and the anomalous spin reconfiguration through the $\text{Ni--O(1)--Ni}$ bonding orbitals connecting the NiO$_2$ planes, which characterize the orbital-selective nature of the bilayer nickelate La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$.
summary: This work uses site-selective $^{17}	ext{O-NMR}$ to probe the spin structure of the bilayer nickelate La3Ni2O7. It reveals a complex interplay between an in-plane Spin Density Wave (SDW) order and the formation of an interlayer spin-singlet state. The findings highlight that the magnetic behavior is highly orbital-selective, with different Ni orbitals governing different types of spin correlations.
main_problem: To investigate the spin structure of the Spin Density Wave (SDW) order and understand the orbital-selective nature of interlayer spin coupling in the bilayer nickelate La3Ni2O7.
main_result: The study reveals the coexistence of SDW order (driven by $d_{x^2-y^2}$ spins) and interlayer spin-singlet formation (governed by $d_{3z^2-r^2}$ spins), characterized by distinct spin configurations at different oxygen sites.
method: Site-selective $^{17}	ext{O-NMR}$ measurements were used to probe the local magnetic environment and spin susceptibility at different oxygen sites within the material.
model_or_system: The physical system is the bilayer nickelate La3Ni2O7. The analysis distinguishes between different oxygen sites (O(1), O(2), O(3,4)) to map out the orbital-selective nature of the magnetic interactions.
key_observables: NMR spectral broadening/shifts, local spin susceptibility ($\chi_{	ext{loc}}^{	ext{spin}}$), and the temperature dependence of the internal magnetic field ($H_{	ext{int}}$) at various O sites.
important_parameters: Transition temperatures $T_{	ext{SDW}} (= 150 	ext{ K})$ and $T_{	ext{A}} (\sim 115 	ext{ K})$; the relative contributions of $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $d_{3z^2-r^2}$ orbitals to magnetism.
main_assumptions: The observed magnetic behavior is interpreted through the lens of orbital-selective spin coupling, distinguishing between in-plane SDW magnetism and interlayer spin-singlet formation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the temperature dependence of the $^{17}	ext{O-NMR}$ spectra, showing peak broadening below $T_{	ext{SDW}}$ and the disappearance of the O(1) signal below $T_{	ext{A}}$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes NMR data across different temperature regimes ($>T_{	ext{SDW}}$, $T_{	ext{SDW}} > T > T_{	ext{A}}$, $T < T_{	ext{A}}$) to map out the evolution of spin order, first establishing the SDW state, then identifying the spin-singlet formation, and finally detailing the anomalous spin reconfiguration below $T_{	ext{A}}$.
why_interesting: The concept of orbital-selective magnetism, where different orbitals participate in different types of magnetic ordering (e.g., SDW vs. spin-singlet), is highly relevant to understanding complex correlated electron physics in cuprates and nickelates.
